{{Short description|Canadian-Serbian mathematician and professor of mathematics}}
{{Use mdy dates|date=December 2022}}
[[File:Portrait Summer 2020..jpg|thumb|Ilijas Farah in 2020]]
'''Ilijas Farah''' (born 18 February 1966) is a Canadian-Serbian<ref>[http://www.mi.sanu.ac.rs/conferences/SetsInSerbia.pdf On Contribution of Serbian Mathematicians to Set Theory]</ref> mathematician and a professor of mathematics at [[York University]] in Toronto and at the Mathematical Institute of Serbian Academy of Sciences and Arts, [[Belgrade]], Serbia.<ref name="MISANU 2016">{{cite web | title=MISANU | website=MISANU | date=May 17, 2016 | url=http://www.mi.sanu.ac.rs | language=la | ref={{sfnref | MISANU | 2016}} | access-date=November 23, 2022}}</ref><ref name="Coskey Farah 2014 pp. 3611–3630">{{cite journal | last1=Coskey | first1=Samuel | last2=Farah | first2=Ilijas | title=Automorphisms of corona algebras, and group cohomology | journal=Transactions of the American Mathematical Society | publisher=American Mathematical Society (AMS) | volume=366 | issue=7 | date=March 19, 2014 | issn=0002-9947 | doi=10.1090/s0002-9947-2014-06146-1 | pages=3611–3630| doi-access=free | arxiv=1204.4839 }}</ref> His research focuses on applications of logic to operator algebras.<ref>{{Google scholar id}}</ref>

==Career==
Farah was born in [[Sremska Mitrovica]], [[Serbia]].  He received his BSc and MSc in 1988 and 1992 respectively from [[Belgrade University]] and his PhD in 1997 from the [[University of Toronto]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu/id.php?id=15997|title=Ilijas Farah - The Mathematics Genealogy Project|website=genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu}}</ref><ref name="sax" /> 

He is a Research Chair in Logic and Operator Algebras at [[York University]], Toronto. Before moving to York University he was an NSERC Postdoctoral Fellow, York University (1997–99), a Hill Assistant Professor at [[Rutgers University]] (1999–2000), and a professor at CUNY–Graduate center and [[College of Staten Island]] (2000–02).<ref name="cv">[http://www.math.yorku.ca/~ifarah/ York University Ilijas Farah Home page]</ref>

Farah was an invited speaker at the [[International Congress of Mathematicians]], [[Seoul]] 2014, section on Logic and Foundations, where he presented his work on applications of logic to operator algebras.<ref>{{Cite conference|conference=Proceedings of the International Congress of Mathematicians, Seoul 2014|volume=II|title=Invited Lectures|editor1=Jang, Sun Young|editor2=Kim, Young Rock|editor3=Lee, Dae-Woong|editor4=Yie, Ikkwon|url=http://www.icm2014.org/download/Proceedings_Volume_II.pdf |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170413065055/http://www.icm2014.org/download/Proceedings_Volume_II.pdf |archive-date=April 13, 2017 |access-date=January 13, 2018}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=ICM2014 VideoSeries IL1.2: Ilijas Farah on Aug15Fri |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=KjkWAIUlk3s |via=YouTube}}</ref>

==Awards, distinctions, and recognitions==
* Sacks prize for the best doctorate in Mathematical Logic, 1997<ref name="sax">{{Cite web|url=https://www.ucl.ac.uk/~ucahcjm/stn/farah/sacks.html|title=1998 Sacks Prize winners announcement|website=ucl.ac.uk}}</ref>
* Governor General's gold medal for one of the two best doctorates at the [[University of Toronto]], 1998
* The Canadian Association for Graduate Studies/University Microfilms International Distinguished Dissertation Award, for the best dissertation in engineering, medicine and the natural sciences in Canada, 1998.
* Dean's award for outstanding research, [[York University]], 2006.<ref name="cv"/>
* Faculty Excellence in Research Award (Established Research Award), Faculty of Science, York University, 2017<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.yorku.ca/science/|title=Faculty of Science - York University|website=Faculty of Science}}</ref>
